issue_title: Site-wide performance regression: TBT up 5–7× and LCP up 20–30% across all pages after 2026-08-07 deploy
issue_body:
## Site-wide performance regression detected — 2026-08-08

Every audited page shows a material performance drop compared to the previous audit (2026-08-07). The pattern of simultaneous TBT explosions across all pages strongly suggests a new render-blocking or long-task script was introduced in the latest deploy.

### Score summary

| Page | Prev perf | Curr perf | Δ | Prev TBT | Curr TBT | Δ TBT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 73 | **53** | **-20** | 137 ms | **405 ms** | **+268 ms** |
| `/projects` | 83 | **65** | **-18** | 58.5 ms | **319.5 ms** | **+261 ms** |
| `/projects/note-structurer` | 90 | **75** | **-15** | 39.5 ms | **199 ms** | **+159.5 ms** |
| `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` | 89 | **79** | **-10** | 39.5 ms | **189 ms** | **+149.5 ms** |
| `/about` | 88 | 83 | -5 | 37 ms | 178.5 ms | +141.5 ms |

Homepage LCP has also worsened: **6.45 s → 8.39 s**.

### Likely causes
1. A large synchronous JavaScript bundle added to the global layout (no code-splitting / deferred loading).
2. A removed dynamic import or lazy-load boundary that previously kept a heavy module off the critical path.
3. A new third-party script loaded eagerly in `<head>`.

### Suggested actions
- [ ] Diff the latest deploy's bundle manifest / build output against the previous one — look for newly inlined or un-split chunks.
- [ ] Run `chrome://tracing` or Lighthouse trace on `/` locally and identify the long task(s) driving TBT above 400 ms.
- [ ] Re-check that the hero image on `/` is preloaded and served in WebP/AVIF — LCP at 8.39 s is the worst recorded value.
- [ ] Consider reverting the deploy if the root cause isn't immediately apparent.

### Visual status
No visual breakage detected; all pages render correctly. The `/about` page remains a content stub (placeholder text only) — pre-existing issue, not caused by this regression.

*Audited at 2026-08-08T08:59:35.705Z*
